en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Gloucester Heights, Haddon Township, Camden County, New Jersey, September 1924, Sheet 20 (Audubon series)

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 of the Sanborn Audubon series, dated September 1924, covers the residential subdivision of Gloucester Heights in Haddon Township, Camden County, at 100 feet to an inch. North points to the left of the sheet. West Nicholson Road runs down the sheet a little right of centre and divides it into two halves. On its north side (left half) a grid of avenues named after colleges, Yale, Princeton, Oxford, Harvard and Rutgers, crosses Lehigh Avenue, with Jefferson Avenue running from Rutgers Avenue to the bottom edge. On the south side (right half) Cornell, Swarthmore, Haverford, University and Temple Avenues run from West Nicholson Road to the right edge, and Yale Avenue is shown dashed as not opened. The shore of Lake Newton curves across the lower left corner, with the compass rose drawn on the water. The blocks are numbered 276 to 296 and are mostly vacant lots with scattered one and two storey frame dwellings, automobile garages and sheds; much of the ground is still undeveloped. Named buildings are Gloucester Heights Public School No. 4 at the corner of West Nicholson Road and Cornell Avenue, the Gloucester Heights Fire Association house on Oxford Avenue, and the Gloucester Heights M.E. Church on West Nicholson Road near Oxford Avenue. A public garage stands on West Nicholson Road between Harvard and Rutgers Avenues. Lot numbers and street widths (40 and 50 feet) are printed along every frontage. The sheet carries its own title, Gloucester Heights, Haddon Township, and a scale bar at the bottom right; there is no index or key map. Neighbouring sheets of the series are not shown and no other sheet of the Audubon atlas is part of this record.
notes: Printed as part of the Audubon, N.J. series (sheet 20, Sept. 1924); catalogued under Gloucester Heights.
Swarthmore Avenue is spelled Swathmore Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
West Nicholson Road on the sheet is Nicholson Road in OpenStreetMap at these junctions.
Yale Avenue south of West Nicholson Road is marked not opened.
Lake Newton is today's Newton Lake.
The area lies in Gloucester City today (parcel municipality code 0414); it was printed as Haddon Township.
